rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A performative promise or one implicitly limited by religious or other impediments creates no problem; an unconditional factual promise raises a truthfulness and prophetic-infallibility difficulty.
rows.anchor: إن الوعد كالوعيد إنشاء لا يحتمل الصدق والكذب

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: In the hadith commentary, the first lapse was forgetfulness, the second was conditional, and the third was deliberate; another narration calls the second deliberate and the third the separation.
rows.anchor: في البخاري وشرحه لابن حجر وكانت الأولى نسيانا والثانية شرطا والثالثة عمدا

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says Moses paired patience with God's will but left obedience unqualified; he fulfilled the qualified promise yet disobeyed by asking, an account al-Alusi criticizes as incomplete.
rows.anchor: وقال القشيري : إن موسى عليه السلام وعد من نفسه بشيئين بالصبر وقرنه بالمشيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds it unlikely Moses would categorically promise patience and obedience after Khidr warned that he would witness apparently objectionable acts; an implicit condition in both clauses resolves the difficulty.
rows.anchor: يبعد من حال موسى عليه السلام القطع بالصبر وعدم عصيان الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because one voluntary act occurs by God's will, all voluntary acts do; the Mu'tazila instead treat the invocation of God's will as devotional, while another theologian argues devotional invocation still has real meaning.
rows.anchor: لأنه إذا صدر بعض الأفعال الاختيارية بمشيئته سبحانه لزم صدور الكل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse has been used to argue that a command entails obligation, but al-Alusi questions that inference; here command means any request, and Moses promises not to disobey any request.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بالآية على أن الأمر للوجوب وفيه نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr permits Moses to follow after his promise; the conditional clause follows from that promise, and Moses must not question any observed act or dispute it before Khidr explains.
rows.anchor: أذن له عليه السلام في الاتباع بعد اللتيا والتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The endpoint may mean Moses should withhold objection until Khidr initiates an explanation, or that questioning should cease permanently after an explanation; both readings imply every act has a wise, good purpose.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجهين فيها إيذان بأن كل ما يصدر عنه فله حكمة وغاية حميدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed causal reading of hatta is not sound.
rows.anchor: وقيل : حتى للتعليل وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read the verb with a hamza and a doubled nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر ( فلا تسئلني ) بالنون المثقلة مع الهمز

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far reads the verb without hamza, with fatḥa on the sīn and lām and a doubled nūn.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي جعفر ( فلا تسلني ) بفتح السين واللام والنون المثقلة من غير همز

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr says all readers retain the final yāʾ; reports differ unusually over whether Ibn Abbas dropped it.
rows.anchor: وكل القراء كما قال أبو بكر بياء في آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pair are Moses and Khidr; Joshua is omitted because he was a follower, though another view says Moses sent him back to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: ولم يضم يوشع عليه السلام لأنه في حكم التبع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the pair walked along the shore, asked a passing ship for passage, and its crew recognized Khidr and carried them without fare.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس مرفوعا أنهما انطلقا يمشيان على ساحل البحر

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: In a report through Abu Hatim, the crew first feared the travelers were thieves and refused; their leader then saw light in their faces and agreed to take them.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي حاتم عن الربيع بن أنس أن أهل السفينة ظنوا أنهم لصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in 'the ship' denotes a generic ship, not one previously identified; reports describe a new, exceptionally sturdy small ferry crossing between shores, with one report placing its route toward Ayla.
rows.anchor: أل فيها لتعريف الجنس إذ لم يتقدم عهد في سفينة مخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An authentic report compares the loss of Moses and Khidr's knowledge to God's knowledge with a bird's tiny loss from the sea.
rows.anchor: صح أنهما حين ركبا جاء عصفور حتى وقع على حرف السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fī with riding here can indicate being inside; another explanation is that riding means entering, as in the wording 'entered the ship'.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن ذلك لإرادة معنى الدخول كأنه قيل حتى إذا دخلا في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe Khidr removing a plank with an adze, driving a peg into the hull, or removing two boards near the waterline.
rows.anchor: فقال له موسى عليه السلام : قوم حملونا بغير نول عمدت إلى سفينتهم فخرقتها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Khidr bored a hole with an awl after the ship reached deep water, then patched it with a board; al-Rabi's report places completion near shore.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس مرفوعا أنهما لما ركبا واطمئنا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports may be reconciled by placing Khidr's initial resolve in deep water and completion of the damage as the ship neared land.
rows.anchor: ويمكن الجمع بأن أول العزم كان وهي في اللج وتمام الفعل كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording places the passengers aboard when the ship was damaged; the lām in Moses' question can mark consequence if he assumes Khidr meant no harm, but causal purpose better fits the rebuke and reply.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم لم يجوز هذا توهما منه أن فيه سوء أدب وليس كذلك

rows.speaker: عبد بن حميد ومسلم وابن مردويه
rows.claim: A report says the ship's other passengers left and Khidr stayed behind to damage it, prompting Moses to object; this seems to conflict with the verse's apparent sequence and passengers aboard.
rows.anchor: قال : فانطلقا حتى إذا ركبا في السفينة فخرج من كان فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proposed reconciliations take the hadith as omitting 'then he damaged it,' or distinguish Khidr's initial intent from the later act and Moses' two objections; the accounts remain difficult to reconcile.
rows.anchor: وهذا ظاهر في أنه عزم على الحرق فاعترض عليه موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation has the travelers leave briefly on an island while Khidr resolves to damage the ship, with Moses objecting before the passengers return and the damage is completed; al-Alusi considers this remote.
rows.anchor: إنه يحتمل أن السفينة لما لججت بهم صادفوا جزيرة في اللج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional sequence does not require the damage to occur immediately after boarding; the consequence must follow and be caused by the condition, not occur at the same time.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن ذلك ليس بلازم وإنما اللازم تسبب الجزاء عن الشرط

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib explicitly says the conditional clause and its consequence need not occur at one time, as in promising tomorrow's honor if someone visits today.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح ابن الحاجب بأنه لا يلزم وقوع الشرط والجزاء في زمان واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some argue a report that the plank was removed as soon as they boarded and the stated endpoint of their journey imply immediate damage; replies treat the report as idiomatic and allow an extended endpoint.
rows.anchor: نعم قال بعضهم : إن خبر لما ركبا في السفينة لم يفجأ إلا والخضر قد قلع لوحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi doubts the authenticity of al-Rabi's report and says the crew likely did not see Khidr damage the ship, since they would have stopped him; al-Qari likewise says they did not see him.
rows.anchor: ثم إن في القلب من صحة رواية الربيع شيئا والله تعالى أعلم بصحتها

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: A non-Prophetic report via Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab says Khidr was visible only to those God allowed to see him, so the crew saw only Moses and could not stop the damage or killing.
rows.anchor: من طريق حماد بن زيد عن شعيب بن الحبحاب أنه قال : كان الخضر عبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rabi also reportedly says the crew later learned Khidr was responsible; Moses likely did not include himself among the ship's people, though the phrase could include passengers.
rows.anchor: نعم سيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى قريبا عن الربيع أيضا أنهم علموا بعد ذلك أنه الفاعل

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Raja read the verb with doubled consonants, expressing intensive causation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء ( لتغرق ) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وزيد بن علي والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وخلف وأبو عبيد وابن سعدان وابن عيسى الأصبهاني
rows.claim: These readers make the ship's people the grammatical subject of 'drown'; on this reading the lām clearly marks consequence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وزيد بن علي والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وخلف وأبو عبيد

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i derives imr from amr meaning abundance; Arabs describe calamities as abundant, and the word denotes a grave, dreadful deed.
rows.anchor: أي داهيا منكرا من أمر الأمر بمعنى كثر قاله الكسائي فأصله كثير

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says Arabic describes calamities as abundant; a second commentator says the expected rhyme with imr was avoided as contrived, citing al-Samaw'al and Abu Dhu'ayb.
rows.anchor: والعرب كما قال ابن جني في سر الصناعة تصف الدواهي بالكثرة

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi relates that Moses became so angry he seized Khidr's clothes and wanted to throw him into the sea; the sea grew rough with Moses' anger, and Joshua reminded him of his covenant.
rows.anchor: وفي الرواية عن الربيع أن موسى عليه السلام لما رأى من الخضر ما رأى امتلأ غضبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's question rebukes Moses for failing to remain patient, and Moses then mastered his impulse.
rows.anchor: وهو متضمن للإنكار على عدم وقوع الصبر منه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses apologizes for forgetting Khidr's instruction; the phrasing assumes Khidr already knows the lapse. A perfect person may be reproached for negligence, not for involuntary forgetfulness itself.
rows.anchor: اعتذار بنسيان الوصية على أبلغ وجه وكأن نسيانه أمر محقق عند الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ may mark cause: forgetfulness remotely caused the failure to follow the instruction, though that failure was the proximate cause of reproach.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الباء للسببية وهي متعلقة بالفعل والنسيان وإن لم يكن سببيا قريبا للمواخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some attach the bāʾ to the sense of a prohibition and take forgetfulness as the reason not to reproach Moses; others say it must mean accompaniment, a view al-Alusi does not accept as necessary.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم تعين كونها للملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may be a relative or descriptive pronoun, but those readings require an implicit noun such as leaving the forgotten instruction, since one is reproached for abandoning it, not for the instruction itself.
rows.anchor: لكن يحتاج هذا ظاهر إلى تقدير مضاف أي بترك ما نسيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most apparent sense is an apology for forgetting the instruction, consistent with the sound report that Moses' first lapse was forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: ثم كون ما ذكر اعتذارا بنسيان الوصية هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Moses did not forget the instruction but used 'forgetfulness' as a tactful pretext, alluding to forgetting something else to avoid a direct lie; Ibn al-Jarir transmits it from Ubayy ibn Ka'b.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا ابن جرير عن أبي بن كعب وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here forgetfulness may mean leaving or neglecting the instruction on the first occasion; 'overburden me' means do not make following you difficult, but ease it by overlooking and not disputing.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون النسيان مجازا عن الترك أي لا تؤاخذني بما تركت من وصيتك

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far reads ʿusran with ḍamma on both consonants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ﴿ عسرا ﴾ بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses accepted the excuse, and the two left the ship walking along the shore, as in the sound report; another narration says they passed through a village.
rows.anchor: الفاء فصيحة أي فقبل عذره فخرجا من السفينة فانطلقا يمشيان على الساحل كما في الصحيح

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Reports name the boy Jaysur, also transmitted with ḥāʾ, or Janabtur; one report says he played among ten boys and was the best-looking and cleanest.
rows.anchor: يزعمون كما قال البخاري أن اسمه جيسور بالجيم وروي بالحاء

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Accounts give several methods of killing: pulling off the boy's head, laying him down and slitting his throat, striking his head against a wall, crushing it with a stone, kicking him, or removing his navel.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخاري في رواية أنه عليه السلام أخذ برأسه من أعلاه فاقتلعه بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the reports of striking, laying down and slitting, and then pulling off the head might be combined sequentially, but considers such harmonization remote.
rows.anchor: وجمع بين الروايات الثلاثة الأول بأنه ضرب رأسه بالجدار أولا ثم أضجعه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take the boy as prepubescent because that is the common literal sense of ghulām; another report from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz says he was twenty.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الغلام لم يكن بالغا لأنه حقيقة الغلام بالشائعة في الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes ghulām literally as a sexually mature youth and child usage as figurative; Layla al-Akhyaliyya and another poet use it of young men.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو حقيقة في البالغ لأن أصله من الاغتلام وهو شدة الشبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' description of the boy as pure supports childhood because adults rarely remain sinless; Ibn Abbas' Prophetic report glosses zakiyya as 'young,' while the adult view says Moses simply had seen no sin from him.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في حديث عن ابن جبير عن ابن عباس مرفوعا تفسير زكية بصغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those arguing that the boy was an adult cite 'without a soul' as evidence of retaliation, reasoning that a child could not be subject to qisas.
rows.anchor: واستدل على كونه بالغا بقوله تعالى ﴿ بغير نفس ﴾ أي بغير حق قصاص لك عليها

rows.speaker: النووي والكرماني
rows.claim: They answer the argument that a child cannot be killed in retaliation: the phrase means killing without right, or singles out retaliation because it suits the context; some scholars say Mosaic law once imposed retaliation for minors.
rows.anchor: وأجاب النووي والكرماني بأن المراد التنبيه على أنه قتله بغير حق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة وابن محيصن وحميد والزهري ونافع واليزيدي وابن مسلم وابن بكير عن يعقوب ورويس عنه أيضا وأبو عبيد وابن جبير الانطاكي وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These authorities read zākiya with a light yāʾ and an alif after zāy; Zayd ibn Ali, al-Hasan, al-Jahdari, Ibn Amir and the Kufans read the intensive zakiyya without alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والأعرج وأبو جعفر وشيبة وابن محيصن وحميد والزهري ونافع

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the intensive adjective zakiyya, formed from an active participle, conveys a stronger, settled quality.
rows.anchor: كما قال أبو حيان يدل على المبالغة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr distinguishes zākiya as never having sinned from zakiyya as having sinned and then been forgiven; al-Alusi finds this distinction unconvincing.
rows.anchor: وفرق أبو عمرو بين زاكية وزكية بأن زاكية بالألف هي التي لم تذنب قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi sees no basis for Abu Amr's distinction: zakā denotes growth and figuratively moral purity; he suggests the alif form may be intransitive and the other passive, making the former stronger for an unpubescent boy.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه فرق غير ظاهر لأن أصل معنى الزكاة النمو والزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either reading intensifies the horror of the act by describing the victim as pure.
rows.anchor: وأياما كان فوصف النفس بذلك لزيادة تفظيع ما فعل

rows.speaker: أبي كعب
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that Moses was terribly startled when Khidr killed the boy and said he had committed an abhorrent deed.
rows.anchor: وقد أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي كعب أن الخضر عليه السلام لما قتل الغلام ذعر موسى

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam defines munkar as what reason rejects and souls recoil from, and considers it more condemnatory than imr; al-Raghib instead defines it as a perilous, difficult unknown.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام المنكر ما أنكرته العقول ونفرت عنه النفوس

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi takes munkar as less severe than imr because the wording moves from the harsher event to the milder one, though al-Kashf says munkar is stronger in diction and in substance.
rows.anchor: واختار الطيبي أنه دون الأمر وقال إن الذي يقتضيه النظم

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf argues that killing directly is more abhorrent than indirectly endangering ship passengers; it rejects a descending-severity inference because the episodes are narrated in chronological order.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أبلغية النكر أما بحسب اللفظ فظاهر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada is reported to hold that munkar is the more emphatic term.
rows.anchor: وروي القول بالابلغية عن قتادة

rows.speaker: صاحب العرس والعرائس
rows.claim: A narrative says the boy's left shoulder was exposed and bore a writing that he would never believe in God; al-Alusi gives it as a report, not an authenticated account.
rows.anchor: حكاه القرطبي عن صاحب العرس والعرائس أن موسى عليه السلام حين قال للخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax foregrounds the murder because it is the more heinous act and Moses' objection is especially apt; this explanation assumes the answer to the conditional is the main clause.
rows.anchor: إنما غير النظم إلى ما ترى لأن القتل أقبح والاعتراض عليه أدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ after meeting the boy implies the killing followed immediately, explaining Moses' instant objection; a delay might have let Khidr learn facts unavailable to Moses.
rows.anchor: وكان العطف بالفاء التعقيبية ليفيد أن القتل وقع عقيب اللقاء من غير ريث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Moses' objection is central in this episode, it is the answer to the conditional, while the killing is part of the condition; in the ship episode the less central objection is independent and Khidr's act is the answer.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أنه لما كان الاعتراض في القصة الثانية معتنى بشأنه وأهم جعل جزاء لإذا الشرطية

rows.speaker: التاشكندي
rows.claim: Al-Tashkandi allows both objections to be independent clauses and makes Khidr's acts the conditional answers, proposing an implicit qad before the second past-tense verb because the killing is more heinous.
rows.anchor: وزعم التاشكندي جواز كون الاعتراضين في القصتين مستأنفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A critic replies that a past affirmative used as a conditional answer with fāʾ requires qad; the acts here are future relative to the condition and need no such link, so the proposed analysis fails.
rows.anchor: بأن الفاء الجزائية لا يجوز أن تدخل على الماضي المثبت إلا بتقدير قد

rows.speaker: ميربادشاه
rows.claim: Mirbadshah says intuitive Arabic resists supplying qad where the context does not require it, and that the issue needing explanation is Moses' renewed objection after his earlier warning.
rows.anchor: وقال ميربادشاه في الرد على ذلك إن الذوق السليم يأبى عن تقدير قد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed rationale says meeting a boy normally calls for pity, not killing, making the killing and objection the focus; a counterargument says boarding a ship normally calls for protecting it, so the contrast is disputed.
rows.anchor: ويقول كما أن لقاء الغلام سبب للرفق لا القتل كذلك ركوب السفينة سبب لحفظها

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: The second supernatural act has become familiar, shifting suspense to whether Moses will honor his promise; therefore his reaction, rather than Khidr's repeated act, is made the conditional answer.
rows.anchor: أن صدور الخوارق عن الخضر عليه السلام خرج بوقوعه مرة مخرج العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A critic says killing's rarity and gravity make it worthy of focus, while an expected objection by any sane person need not be; al-Alusi replies that rare events are especially striking and the objection still merits attention.
rows.anchor: وإنكار ذلك مكابرة فمراد الشيخ أن كون القتل أقبح من مبادىء قلة صدوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi favors the Sheikh's rationale because it works whether killing or damaging the ship is judged worse; it also fits the story's overall focus on Moses, though the first episode departs from that pattern to satisfy anticipation.
rows.anchor: وقد رجح بذلك على ما تقدم واستأنس له أيضا بأن مسلق الكلام من أوله لشرح حال موسى

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر وابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر وشيبة وطلحة ويعقوب وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: These readers pronounce nukan with ḍamma on both consonants wherever it is accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر وابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر وشيبة وطلحة ويعقوب وأبو حات

none: Volume transition and heading only; no commentary point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added word laka sharpens Khidr's confrontation over Moses' repeated refusal to heed the instruction and his failure to deliberate; the second act increased his disapproval despite the reminder.
rows.anchor: زيادة ( لك ) لزيادة المكافحة على رفض الوصية وقلة التثبت والصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses means that if he questions any further marvel after this episode or question, Khidr should end their companionship.
rows.anchor: بعد هذه المرة أو بعد هذه المسألة

rows.speaker: عيسى ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read the verb with fatḥa on tāʾ, meaning 'do not be my companion'; another reading from Isa has ḍamma on tāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ, with the sense 'do not keep me as your companion.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى ويعقوب ( فلا تصحبني ) بفتح التاء من صحبة

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-A'raj reads with fatḥa on tāʾ and bāʾ and a doubled nūn, intensifying the prohibition to mean 'never be my companion'; this supports a firm command to separate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج ( فلا تصحبني ) بفتح التاء والباء وشد النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended prohibition is firm separation, not permission for Khidr to abandon Moses if another question occurs; one grammarian's proposed second object, 'your knowledge,' is rejected.
rows.anchor: والمراد به الحزم بالترك والمفارقة لا الترخيص على معنى إن سألتك بعد

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi explains that Moses had reached the point at which Khidr could justifiably leave him because he had repeatedly violated their agreement.
rows.anchor: وقال النووي : معناه قد بلغت إلى الغاية التي تعذر بسببها في فراقي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: An authentic Prophetic report asks God's mercy for Moses and says that, had he been patient, he would have seen wonders; shame at his companion led Moses to speak.
rows.anchor: وصح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : رحمة الله علينا وعلى موسى

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم
rows.claim: They read min ladunni with a light nūn; most grammarians say the protective nūn is omitted while the original genitive nūn remains, though an alternative treats lad as a nūn-less dialect form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم ( من لدنى ) بتخفيف النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative that the surviving nūn is protective is challenged because such a nūn guards a consonant built on sukūn from kasra; its defenders say it may instead guard the final ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن نون الوقاية إنما هي في المبني على السكون لتقيه الكسر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid calls the light-nūn reading a bad error, but al-Alusi suggests he meant a faulty transmission, since lad with fatḥa or sukūn is documented as a dialect.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : سوء غلط ولعله أراد رواية

rows.speaker: عيسى وأبي
rows.claim: Isa reads ʿudhran with ḍamma on the dhāl; a reading from Ubayy adds the possessive yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى ( عذرا ) بضم الذال ورويت عن أبي عمرو وعن أبي ( عذرى )

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority identify the town as Antioch, reported by al-Tha'labi from Ibn Abbas; other reports name Barqa, Bajrawan, Apulla, Nazareth, or a town in the Andalusian Green Island.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على أنها أنطاكية وحكاه الثعلبي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar says no identification can be trusted; this dispute is as unreliable as attempts to identify the meeting of the two seas.
rows.anchor: قال ابن حجر : والخلاف هنا كالخلاف في مجمع البحرين ولا يوثق بشيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith describes the townspeople as vile.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث أتيا أهل قرية لئاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers reading 'they asked its people for food' as a clause describing the town; making it a clause about the people or the answer to 'when' is possible grammatically but misses the intended focus.
rows.anchor: والوصفية مختار المحققين كما ستعلمه إن شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: السبكي
rows.claim: Al-Subki answers al-Safadi's question by listing the only three grammatical analyses and arguing that the town-description is required: an answer clause would make asking for food the point, while a people-description shifts focus from the town.
rows.anchor: فأجاب السبكي بأن جملة ( استطعما ) محتملة لأن تكون في محل جر صفة لقرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred reading, the text stresses that the town itself had blameworthy residents who denied travelers' hospitality; the grammar requires 'its people' because the described noun is town, not people.
rows.anchor: فيتعين الأول ويجب فيه ( استطعما أهلها ) ولا يجوز استطعماهم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated noun may cover everyone in the town: Moses and Khidr asked its residents in succession, and none offered hospitality; repeating 'its people' rather than a pronoun signals total coverage and heightens their blame.
rows.anchor: فأتى بالظاهر إشعارا بتأكيد العموم فيه وأنهما لم يتركا أحدا من أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second group called 'its people' could be the same residents, different residents, or a mixture; the wording also allows the travelers to have entered and questioned the town gradually.
rows.anchor: أن الأهل الثاني يحتمل أن يكونوا هم الأولون أو غيرهم أو منهم ومن غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun repetition suggests that God's servants were treated well despite the town's refusal, and that God does not punish everyone for some people's misdeeds; a pronoun would require the same people both times.
rows.anchor: وأبى ومع ذلك قوبلوا بأحسن الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that the noun is repeated to avoid two adjacent pronouns, since the Qur'an and eloquent Arabic freely use such constructions.
rows.anchor: حتى سمعت عن شخص أنه قال : إن العدول عن استطعماهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the asking clause is the answer to 'when,' it follows arrival; if it describes the town, the arrival may have occurred earlier, showing hunger did not make the travelers avoid a good purpose.
rows.anchor: ومن تمام الكلام فيما ذكر أن استطعما أن جعل جوابا فهو متأخر عن الاتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection proposes the shorter wording 'when they came to a town, they asked its people for food'; mentioning the people at arrival emphasizes that they entered the town intending to ask and were refused, intensifying the villagers' meanness.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه جيء بالأهل للإشارة إلى أنهم قصدوا بالإتيان في قريتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting 'its people' would lose the point: Arabic associates coming with a place or its inhabitants, while asking a town is only figurative, so that construction is not equivalent to the verse.
rows.anchor: إن الإتيان ينسب إلى للمكان كأتيت عرفات ولمن فيه كأتيت أهل بغداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the story that the townspeople offered gold to change the Quranic word, noting that another version places the tale in Ali's time and that it has no basis.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم يحكي وقوع هذه القصة في زمن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه ولا أصل لشيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the two occurrences refer to different groups; a report from Abu Hurayra says men refused and a Berber woman eventually fed them, and a similar view is attributed to al-Shafi'i.
rows.anchor: قال : أطعمتها امرأة من بربر بعد أن طلبا من الرجال فلم يطعموهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two-group theories conflict with the usual force of repeating a definite noun, which here adds condemnation; on an emphatic reading, the term may denote residents from whom hospitality would normally be expected.
rows.anchor: وأورد عليهما أن فيهما مخالفة لما هو الغالب في إعادة الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some who reject customary assumptions take the travelers to have asked all residents because they were in need; the clause 'they found' coordinates with their arrival.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يحكم العادة يقول : إنهما عليهما السلام أتوا الجميع وسألوهم لما أنهما على ما قيل قد مستهما الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They found the wall on a cold night, with no lodging, beside the road; inqad means it was about to fall, perhaps rapidly like a meteor, or to crumble into gravel.
rows.anchor: روي أنهما التجآ إليه حيث لم يجدا مأوى وكانت ليلتهما ليلة باردة

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: The author of al-Lawamiḥ derives inqad from small stones or gravel and takes the wall to be about to crumble into pebbles.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب اللوامح : هو من الفضة وهي الحصى الصغار

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali analyzes inqad on the afʿal pattern from naqd; al-Suhayli calls that analysis mistaken.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو علي في الإيضاح أن وزنه أفعل من النقض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'The wall wants to collapse' figuratively means it is near collapse, by metonymy of cause or a metaphor comparing nearness to inclination; Arabic commonly attributes human acts to inanimate things.
rows.anchor: والمراد من إرادة السقوط قربه من ذلك على سبيل المجاز المرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry illustrates personification: a spear 'wants' a man's chest, time 'intends' kindness (Hassan), and Abu Nuwas has a lute speak; the usage is too common to need proof.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قوله : يريد الرمح صدر أبي براء

rows.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن داود الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Ibn Dawud reportedly denied metaphor in the Qur'an and interpreted 'wants' as referring to Khidr or Moses, or as literal life and will created in the wall; al-Alusi calls these strained and destructive of the rhetoric.
rows.anchor: أنه ينكر وقوع المجاز في القرآن فيؤول الآية بأن الضمير في يريد للخضر

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan doubts that the denial of metaphor is truly attributed to Ibn Dawud, given his standing as an accomplished poet and prose writer.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : لعل النقل لا يصح عن الرجل وكيف يقول ذلك

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading makes the wall 'be broken' in the passive; the readings attributed to Abd Allah and al-A'mash add lām and an implied subjunctive particle.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( ينقض ) بضم الياء وفتح القاف والضاد مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: علي وعكرمة وخليد بن سعد ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: They read yanqāṣ with ṣād, a form meaning to crack or break; Ibn Khalawayh cites an Arab expression for a tooth splitting lengthwise, and Dhu al-Rumma uses manqāṣ for a wild bull.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعكرمة وخليد بن سعد ويحيى بن يعمر ( ينقاص ) بالصاد

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri has a reading with a long vowel and ḍād; the common interpretation of the variants is that the wall was collapsing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري ( ينقاض ) بألف وضاد معجمة والمشهور تفسيره بينهدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
rows.claim: They say Khidr smoothed the wall with his hand until it stood; al-Qurtubi calls this the soundest account and most fitting to prophetic practice.
rows.anchor: مسحه بيده فقام كما روي عن ابن عباس وابن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics say an effortless repair would not merit wages; the reply is that achieving the needed result can merit compensation even if it was easy for the worker.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأنه غير ملائم لما بعد إذ لا يستحق بمثله الأجر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Other accounts say Khidr propped the wall with a pillar, plastered it, or demolished and rebuilt it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أقامته بعمود عمده به وقال مقاتل : سواه بالشيد

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report in Ibn al-Anbari's codex collection, attributed to the Prophet, reads that Khidr demolished the wall and then sat down to rebuild it.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قرأ ( فوجد فيها جدارا يريد أن ينقض فهدمه

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says the wall was one hundred cubits high; another report gives dimensions of two hundred cubits high, five hundred long and fifty wide, beside a road where people feared passing.
rows.anchor: وكان طول هذا الجدار إلى السماء على ما نقل النووي عن وهب بن منبه مائة ذراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reads Moses' words as urging Khidr to take payment so they could recover and sustain themselves; it also asks why he declined wages. Another view treats the remark as criticism of gratuitous work for people who denied them hospitality.
rows.anchor: تحريضا للخضر عليه السلام وحثا على أخذ الجعل والأجرة على فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says etakhadha derives from the root takhadha, with the first tāʾ radical and the second inflectional, following the Basran analysis; other grammarians derive it from akhadha and explain the form as altered by frequent use.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب البصريين وقال غيرهم : إنه الاتخاذ افتعال من الأخذ

rows.speaker: عبد الله والحسن وقتادة وأبو بحرية وابن محيصن وحميد واليزيدي ويعقوب وأبو حاتم وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers use lattaḫiḏta, with an open initial tāʾ and kasra on the khāʾ, meaning 'you would have taken'; some readers pronounce the dhāl clearly and others assimilate it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والحسن وقتادة وأبو بحرية وابن محيصن وحميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase adds the source noun to an adverbial of place by broad usage; Ibn al-Hajib instead treats the relation as meaning 'in,' as discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: على إضافة المصدر إلى الظرف اتساعا وابن الحاجب يجعل الإضافة في مثله على معنى في

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads firaq with nunation and makes bayna accusative as an adverb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ( فراق بيني ) بالتنوين ونصب بين على الظرفية

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says 'between me and you' replaces 'between us' for emphasis, concrete separation, the present time of separation, or the third objection that caused it.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : والعدول عن بيننا لمعنى التأكيد والإشارة إلى الفراق

rows.speaker: العلامة الأول
rows.claim: The first commentator says this last objection caused separation because the first two exposed apparent wrongs and were excusable, whereas repairing a wall for an inhospitable town is a kindness.
rows.anchor: إنما كان هذا سبب الفراق دون الأولين لأن ظاهرهما منكر فكان معذورا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Moses objected to the ship and boy for God's sake, but objected to the wall for himself and worldly need; al-Kashf rejects this as unworthy of both prophets and possibly inauthentic.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما في وجهه أن قول موسى عليه السلام في السفينة

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri transmits a similar explanation distinguishing Moses' earlier God-centered objections from the self-interested objection about the wall; the author rejects it as unsuitable to their rank.
rows.anchor: وحكى القشيري نحوه عن بعضهم ورد ذلك في الكشف بأنه لا يليق بجلالتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of spiritual interpretation treat the episodes as lessons for Moses: his past experiences included being set adrift in the ark, killing an Egyptian, and watering Shu'ayb's daughters without payment.
rows.anchor: عن أرباب المعاني أن هذه الأمور التي وقعت لموسى مع الخضر حجة على موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reports a purported retort from Khidr connecting those episodes to Moses breaking the tablets, killing the Egyptian, and watering the flock unpaid, but says such reports are unsound and the cases differ; Khidr would not argue this way to Moses.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن شيئا من ذلك لا يصح والفرق ظاهر بين ما صدر من موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abu Abd Allah, perhaps al-Malati, gives Khidr's advice: be useful and cheerful, avoid harm and anger, abandon disputation, go only when needed, and reproach your own errors rather than another's.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي الدنيا والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان وابن عساكر عن أبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: يوسف بن أسباط
rows.claim: Yusuf ibn Asbat says he heard that Khidr advised Moses to learn in order to act, not merely to speak; when Moses asked for a prayer, Khidr prayed that God ease his obedience. Al-Alusi doubts the report's authenticity.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وابن عساكر عن يوسف بن أسباط قال بلغني : أن الخضر

rows.speaker: ابن أبي وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Waththab reads the verb without hamza, articulating the yāʾ plainly; the sīn marks emphasis because the explanation is immediate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي وثاب ( سانبيك ) بإخلاص الياء من غير همز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading is that Moses did not ask for an explanation; another report says he grabbed Khidr's clothes and insisted on learning what authorized the acts, prompting Khidr's answer.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا لم يكن عن طلب من موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl here means the outcome and eventual consequence, not the interpretive act of returning something to its source; it refers to the ship's rescue, the parents' rescue and replacement, and the orphans' treasure.
rows.anchor: والتأويل رد الشيء إلى مآله والمراد به هنا المآل والعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the explanation 'what you could not bear patiently' rather than simply what Khidr did both reproaches Moses and may increase his attention to what follows.
rows.anchor: نوع تعريض به عليه السلام وعتاب ويجوز أن يقال : إن ذلك لاستشارة مزيد توجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣabran is the direct object of tastatiʿ, while ʿalayhi is advanced for the sake of the verse ending.
rows.anchor: و ( صبرا ) مفعول تستطع وعليه متعلق به وقدم رعاية للفاصلة
